subject.title: Feature: config-level default task notify policy

question: Should OpenClaw add a public config-level default task notify policy, and should that contract be a single global default or a per-runtime policy map?
rationale: This would add new user-visible configuration that changes message delivery behavior across ACP, subagent, and Task Flow paths, so automation should not choose the public contract or default semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define one core config contract
options.body: Add a narrow agents.defaults.tasks surface that preserves unset behavior, lets explicit notifyPolicy values win, and supports the runtime granularity maintainers choose.

options.title: Handle only narrower runtime issues
options.body: Leave this broad config request open or defer it while addressing Discord, Codex mirror, and ACP runaway notification behavior separately.

options.title: Reject a new config surface
options.body: Close this direction after documenting that per-task notify updates and targeted runtime fixes are the supported policy surfaces.

recommendation.title: Define one core config contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow agents.defaults.tasks surface that preserves unset behavior, lets explicit notifyPolicy values win, and supports the runtime granularity maintainers choose.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the task delivery and ACP/subagent executor refactors that own the current policy resolution path.
